description:
FILED s402 (Opus 5), found by task #339 amendment (iv) — the ref='' probe the
ruling asked for BEFORE moving the drop announcement.  Two of the three ref=''
sites are legitimate declines (comp/final_line_num.t is DELIBERATELY invalid
Perl — `print 1+` at EOF; op/closure.t is a `format` block, blessed
not-supported).  The third is this bug.

=== THE BUG (silent wrong, two flavours) ==================================

A bare `/PATTERN/` match as the FIRST argument of a PAREN-LESS call is
tokenized by PPI as DIVISION, so PCL never sees a match:

    sub ok { print "ok(@_)\n" }   my $qr = qr/foo/;   $_ = "foofoo";

    ok /$qr/, "desc";      perl: ok(1 desc)      PCL: (nothing — statement dropped)
    ok /foo/, "desc";       perl: ok(1 desc)      PCL: (nothing)
    ok /foo/;               perl: ok(1)           PCL: (nothing)
    print /foo/, "\n";      perl: 1               PCL: (nothing)
    foo /foo/, "d";         perl: foo(1 d)        PCL: (nothing)
    ok /foo/ ? 1 : 0;       perl: ok(1)           PCL: (nothing)
  WORSE — with a modifier letter it compiles to real DIVISION and CRASHES:
    ok /foo/x, "d";         perl: ok(1 d)         PCL: (P-/ (P-/ ...) "x")
                                                    -> division-by-zero at run time
  INVERSE (all work today):
    ok(/$qr/, "desc");   ok m/$qr/, "d";   ok $_ =~ /$qr/, "d";
    ok !/bar/, "d";     grep /foo/, @a;     return /foo/;

=== WHY (PPI, not PCL) ====================================================

perl expects a TERM after a bareword that is not a known unary operator, so
`/` starts a match.  PPI already does this after `grep`, `return`, `(` and
`=`, and gets it wrong after every other Word — INCLUDING core list operators
(`print`):

  ok /x/, 1;      Word(ok)    Operator(/) Word(x) Operator(/) Operator(,) Number(1)
  grep /x/, @a;   Word(grep)  Regexp::Match(/x/)  Operator(,) Symbol(@a)   <- right

Logged upstream-style in docs/ppi-upstream-bugs.md §11, with a FAILING row in
docs/ppi-bug-report.t (Bug 8, tests => 8).  PPI 1.291 / perl 5.40.3.

=== POPULATION ============================================================

Static: the ref='' announcements name t/re/pat_re_eval.t (line 1114,
`ok /$qr/,  "RT #132772 - compile time qr//"`) and t/re/pat.t; the census
(docs/parse-error-drop-census-s399.tsv) counts those drops under "Handle
single node of unknown type".  NOT measured file-by-file yet — the new drop
announcement (task #339, s402) prints file+line+text for every one, so
`tools/gate-set-scan.pl`-style stderr collection over both populations now
gives the exact list in one pass.  Do that FIRST; it is the sizing.

=== WHERE THE FIX BELONGS =================================================

The raw-token-stream repair family in Pl/Parser2.pm (`_repair_swallowing_
prototypes`, `_repair_alias_foreach`, `_repair_nary_foreach` — the §7b/§10
pattern in ppi-upstream-bugs.md): no tree edit can work, because the pattern
text has already been re-tokenized as code, so the repair must re-lex the run.
The CONDITION must be perl's own (a `/` in TERM position: after a Word that is
neither a term nor a named unary — mind `$x / 2`, `time / 60`, and a Word that
IS a constant), which is why this is a task and not a one-line guard.
Probe the breaking case (feedback_probe_the_breaking_case): every
`WORD / EXPR` division spelling in both populations.

=== RULED s403 (Fable, docs/fable-answers-s402.md §4) ===
The repair's condition = the compiler's EXISTING callable classifier (#266:
"a bare NAME is a CALL only where it is CALLABLE" — list-op builtin or user
sub without a `()` prototype); NEVER a new word list beside it (rule 11).
Layer = Parser2 `_repair_*`, never the $end_pars region.  Size for free in
session B's measurement pass (grep the announcement lines over both
populations); queue by count — first filler after B unless a real sweep row
is affected.  #354 (`)*name` glob mis-lex) is the same family and may share
the commit if the condition is genuinely shared ("after a term-ending token").


SIZED s404 (session B by-product, docs/opus5-review-requests-s404.md §8): one
transpile pass over BOTH populations with PCL_DROP_ANNOUNCE=all (657 files,
2.5 min, 388 announcement lines).

  #351's shape = 6 announcements in 3 files, ALL in perl's own t/:
    t/re/pat.t lines 99, 101, 105, 114   (`ok /re/, qq[...]`)
    t/re/pat_advanced.t:1343             (`ok /A (*THEN) X | B (*THEN) C/x`)
    t/re/pat_re_eval.t:1360              (`ok /$qr/, "RT #132772 ..."`)
  ZERO in perl-tests/ (the sweep population) and zero in lib/.

So by the s403 ruling's own test NO real sweep row is affected: #351 stays
the first filler after session B, it does not jump ahead of #346.

Related but DIFFERENT keyword, same PPI family, worth covering with it:
t/op/switch.t:836 `when /pea/` (also dropped).

NOT #351, though it looks like it: perl-tests/split.t:503 (and its t/op/split.t
twin) `my ($sp) = grep /\s/u, map chr, reverse 128 .. 255 ... or skip '...'`.
The statement transpiles FINE in isolation (probed) — its drop is the
`funcall`-reference "Missing case" and it is blessed in the census.


DONE s404 (commit a46aa3f).  _repair_word_match rewrites the opening `/` to
`m/` on the raw token stream and reparses.  The condition is perl's own and is a
NEGATIVE — "the previous Word is not a TERM" — which is what makes it safe:
measured on perl 5.40.3, `/` after a bareword is division ONLY for a term
(`time / 60`, `use constant PI => 6; PI / 2` = 3, `sub g () {…}; g / 2` = 5);
for a non-term perl does not fall back to division, it is a SYNTAX ERROR.  PCL
assumes valid Perl, so "not a term" is the whole test.  Term sources: the 0-ary
builtins from the ONE arity table (never a new word list — rule 11), a
`use constant`/`sub NAME ()` in the document, and the ALL-CAPS constant
convention the compiler already uses elsewhere.

BREAKING CASE the population scan found (this is why it was run): `map { … }
<op/*>` — PPI derails the GLOB into `< Word / * >`, and a repair there would be
catastrophic.  Hence the `<` guard.  28 `WORD /` sites over both populations:
`ok`, `while`, `when` repair; that one must not.

RESULT: 11 dropped statements recovered (announcement census 388 -> 377);
emission moves in exactly 3 files, all in perl's t/; corpus-diff identical, so
the sweep could not move.  Companion --dir re: pat_re_eval.t 461 -> 462 failing
rows — a statement that used to vanish now reports honestly.

RULE 13 done: ppi-upstream-bugs.md §11 gains the workaround section,
ppi-bug-report.t Bug 8 was already there, canary in Pl/t/misc-fixes-02.t.
subject: PPI mis-lexes a bare /PATTERN/ after a paren-less call as DIVISION: `ok /$qr/, "desc"` is silently dropped (and `/foo/x` compiles to real division)
